$comment: Audited inventory of every outbound target reachable from site/. site/ is a committed build artifact whose editor sources are not in any public repository, so a rebuild can silently add, drop or re-point a network target and nothing in the tree would notice. Check 9 (outbound egress) requires every http(s) URL literal in site/ to appear here and classifies it, requires every entry under 'forbidden' to be absent, and re-derives each declared integrity pin from the repository's own files. Anything new fails the publish gate until a human classifies it.
$how: Built from a whole-tree scan on 2026-09-20 with the same file filter check 9 uses (site/**/*.{js,mjs,cjs,html,htm,css,webmanifest,json,svg}, files <= 8 MiB). URL literals were extracted, then each one was sliced and read in context before being classified. 'reachable: false' means the literal is present in the bundle but no code path in this application can turn it into a request; the evidence field says why.

$roles.namespace: XML/JSON namespace URI or schema id. Never requested; XML/JSON parsers treat it as an opaque identifier.
$roles.doc-only: Appears inside a string that is only logged, thrown or displayed. No call site turns it into a request.
$roles.user-link: Rendered as an href for a human to click. No request happens until the reader clicks it.
$roles.remote-script: Fetched and then executed as JavaScript in the application's origin. This is the only class that can change the application's behaviour, so it is the only class subject to an integrity pin.
$roles.self-reference: The deployed URL of this very site, recorded in a manifest the application reads.
$roles.loopback-placeholder: A localhost base URL that only the no-window (server-render) branch of a template literal can select. The static deploy always runs with a window, so the branch is unreachable here.
$roles.forbidden: Must not appear anywhere in site/. Presence is a finding.

targets.evidence: assets/src-CMkpkg0p.js -- fetched by Dt() and executed from a Blob URL. This is the fallback the browser executor uses when the self-hosted /spice-simulator/vendor/ngspice.js cannot be fetched. Pin value corrected: the earlier hand analysis called @0.0.0 a mutable tag, but npm rejects a republish of an existing version and 0.0.0 is the package's only published version (dist-tags: latest=0.0.0), so the reference is immutable. What was missing is the integrity check, which repairs.ngspice-cdn-integrity adds.

integrity.enforcedBy: the application's own Rt() helper (globalThis.crypto.subtle.digest('SHA-256', ...)), called from Dt(); a mismatch throws instead of executing the payload
integrity.whyAsserted: the pin is a literal this repository owns, and the artifact it must match -- site/vendor/ngspice.js -- is in the same repository. Re-deriving the pin from that file on every run means the two can never drift apart: replacing the self-hosted engine fails the guard until the pin is re-derived.
integrity.provenance: The CDN artifact and site/vendor/ngspice.js are byte-identical (7,211,245 bytes, same sha256), so the fallback is a mirror of the asset we ship, not an independent build. The pin is therefore exactly the hash of our own file. Text-vs-bytes equivalence was verified before pinning: sha256(raw bytes) == sha256(utf8(text(bytes))) for this artifact, which is what the app's helper computes.

verified.method: npm registry GET /@o.z%2Fngspice-wasm for versions; downloaded the jsDelivr artifact and hashed it; hashed site/vendor/ngspice.js
verified.result: versions=[0.0.0], latest=0.0.0; CDN sha256 == vendor sha256 == the pinned hex

targets.evidence: site/index.html and site/404.html -- the bare origin named by the shell's Content-Security-Policy in script-src and connect-src. It is the same origin as the target above and exists for the same reason: the browser executor must still be able to load and fetch the ngspice fallback when the self-hosted /spice-simulator/vendor/ngspice.js cannot be reached. Listing it here is not a formality -- check 11 refuses any origin in the policy that the manifest does not classify, so the allowlist cannot grow without an audit. What may actually EXECUTE from this origin is constrained by the SHA-256 pin, not by the policy: the policy decides whether the request is allowed at all, repairs.ngspice-cdn-integrity decides whether the bytes are ours.

verified.method: the origin of the pinned artifact target above; no separate request is made to the bare origin
verified.result: same origin as https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@o.z/ngspice-wasm@0.0.0/ngspice.js, whose bytes were downloaded and hashed

forbidden.why: The target repository is private (docs/REPO_LAYOUT.md records Visibility=Private as intentional; the public GitHub API returns 404 for it). Every anonymous visitor who pressed the product's only feedback control landed on a 404. Replaced by the public repository's new-issue URL; re-introducing it is a finding.

repairs.why: The 'Report bug' control prefills a public GitHub issue and its own copy says the issue will be public, but the URL pointed at a private repository. Re-point it at the public repository that hosts this deploy.

The fallback loader fetches a third-party script and executes it in the application's origin with no integrity check. Verify the payload against a SHA-256 that equals the hash of the engine we self-host, and refuse to execute on mismatch.

runtimeProbe.marker: ngspice WASM failed its SHA-256 pin
runtimeProbe.why: scripts/egress-integrity.mjs lifts these two functions out of the shipped chunk and runs them, so the fail-closed branch is proven by execution rather than by a string match. The names are minified and belong to this artifact revision; a rebuild that renames them makes the probe exit 3 instead of passing quietly.
